geometry_edits.rationale: Change the single bar into a split-wing composition to create a legible public threshold and reduce box-like sealing.
Align the split with the long axis so the mass still reads as one dominant body.
Keep the pieces legible as one building through a connector.
Preserve a ground-level public relation at the access edge.
Introduce a usable void proportion rather than a decorative seam.
Attach a courtyard to the dominant mass so the ground threshold becomes publicly legible.
Make the new void-bearing composition the compiled root while preserving the primary mass in ancestry.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the simple bar with a split-wing massing so the ground plane can open to a public threshold rather than remain a sealed extrusion.
Keep the dominant bar longitudinally organized while enabling a readable split across the site depth.
Introduce a connective hinge so the split reads as one dominant gesture instead of disconnected pieces.
Preserve an active ground relation along the frontage rather than lifting the full bar away from the street.
Open a substantial but still compact public seam/court that can serve as the required threshold.
Add a true void tied to the primary mass so the access edge resolves into usable public space.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single coherent mass in every view, but it is too generic and too sealed for the neighborhood-living brief. The blue frontage edge is answered only weakly: there is no legible public void, court, seam, or undercut aligned to the access side, so the ground condition fails the active-edge invariant. The object also behaves like a box with a light roof bend rather than a massing that clearly supports mixed-use ground/public threshold + calmer upper hierarchy. The silhouette is not stair-like, but that is not the issue; the issue is that the bend is too slight to register as a meaningful section or program move. It is repair-integral and not visibly self-colliding, but it lacks the carved/public ground logic required by the brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and civic; useful for void/threshold logic, not for copying its sculptural roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Strong carved central void with a calm, continuous upper mass and a readable public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More complex campus composition than this candidate; do not imitate the fragmentation if the current mass needs a simpler street bar.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a large courtyard and bridges can organize mixed program while keeping a dominant mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is much more object-like and retail-scaled; transfer the entry/ground response, not the overall typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact low-rise volume can gain program legibility through a clear entry canopy and a simple grounded threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual for a different program and section logic; its terrace-tower strategy is not appropriate here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped housing massing can preserve a strong silhouette while organizing terraces and long-span relationships.

warnings: Visible mass appears coherent but semantically underdeveloped for program_context.
